documentation: Console I/O and java.io.File extensions. println()/print()/readLine() are real kotlin.io declarations (not kotlin package members, despite how commonly they're used) — moved here from kotlin.json where they'd been misclassified earlier in this manifest's history.

declarations.name: println
limitations: Real println takes 0 or 1 argument; this passes every argument through to Lua's print() comma-joined, so a multi-arg call compiles but has no real Kotlin equivalent to match against

declarations.name: print
limitations: Only the first argument is read (io.write(arg0)); a 2nd+ argument is silently dropped, though real Kotlin print() never had one to begin with

declarations.name: readLine
limitations: No dedicated codegen and no matching Lua global — compiles to a call to an undefined global, fails at runtime

declarations.name: readln
limitations: Same as readLine() — no dedicated codegen

declarations.name: readText
limitations: No File type exists in this subset at all — no filesystem API of any kind

declarations.name: use
limitations: No Closeable type exists in this subset
